rationale: Moskva crew rescued: 396 vs 58.

rationale: South Korean and British estimates of about 6,000 North Korean casualties differ from HUR's more than 7,000.

rationale: The 3rd Corps claims 125 km² in Vivaldi, analysts more than 200 and mappers about 240 km².

rationale: Ukrainian troops' 5:1 (8-9:1 at worst) shell ratio in early February 2024 conflicts with officials' 1:10 for February 2024.

resolution: Ihnat likely counted the 4 Zircon or other aeroballistic missiles as ballistic.

rationale: For the same night, the Air Force counts 74 missiles launched and the Defence Ministry 77.
resolution: The Defence Ministry gave rounded figures and may count missile categories differently, e.g. 25 rather than 28 ballistic or hypersonic.

rationale: OSINT puts Vivaldi phase 1 at over 200 km², while the corps claims 75 km² cleared plus 10 km² liberated.

rationale: The corps claims 125 km² retaken in Vivaldi, while mappers put the area at 200–240 km².
resolution: The corps counts only formally cleared or liberated ground; outside OSINT mappers count all area where Russian control ended, including grey zone.

rationale: Magura hits on the Ivanovets: six vs three.

rationale: The computed DeepState net of 36 km² and Radio Svoboda's 27 km² for July 2026 conflict.
resolution: Radio Svoboda's figure is likely an error or a different source; DeepState's own report also gives 36 km².

rationale: Observers saw about a hundred Russian troops emerge from the Sudzha pipeline on 8 March 2025, while Gerasimov claimed over 600 took part.

rationale: Radio Svoboda's 27 km² and DeepState's published 36 km² for Russian gains in July 2026 conflict.
resolution: Radio Svoboda's figure is likely an error or a different source; DeepState's own report and the computed series give 36 km².

rationale: Ukrainian troops at Avdiivka reported 5:1 in early 2024 while another report gives 1:10 at Avdiivka in February 2024.
resolution: Anecdotal ratios from different sectors and days; 8–9:1 at worst is close to 10:1.

rationale: Ukrainian gains in Dec 2025: 21 km² (DeepState) vs 305 km² (ISW).

rationale: Russia's claimed 6,000 km² of 2025 gains conflicts with DeepState's 4,336 km² and CSIS's 4,831 km².

rationale: The NIS put North Korean dead at about 600 in April 2025, while a BBC analysis counted 2,304 killed.
resolution: Different methods and probably different dates; the NIS figure is an early official estimate.

rationale: Mariupol garrison size: up to 4,400 vs more than 8,000.

rationale: Length of the Kupiansk pipeline route: about 10 km vs 15 km.

rationale: Avdiivka infiltration pipe length: nearly 2 km vs 3.7 km.

rationale: The computed DeepState net of +36 km² and Radio Svoboda's 27 km² for July 2026 conflict.
resolution: Radio Svoboda's figure is likely an error or a different source; DeepState's own report also gives 36 km².

rationale: Net Russian gain for November 2024 is 700+ km² (DeepState) vs about 627 km² (ISW).
resolution: Different trackers: DeepState and ISW map control differently and use different cut-off dates.

rationale: Ukrainian sources give different daily glide-bomb counts for Avdiivka in February 2024: about 60 versus 80–110.
resolution: Different observers and days: unit reports of a typical daily rate versus Foka's figure, possibly a peak or a wider sector.

rationale: Murz put lost Russian equipment at Avdiivka at 300 units, while Naalsio had visually counted 574 Russian vehicles lost by 27 January 2024.
resolution: Murz's is an informal milblogger figure, likely of irrecoverable armour only; Naalsio counts every visually confirmed vehicle loss, damaged ones included.

rationale: Morozov's 300 units of lost equipment is less than half of Naalsio's 690 visually confirmed Russian vehicles at Avdiivka.
resolution: Morozov may count only irrecoverable armour or use an earlier cut-off; Naalsio includes abandoned and damaged vehicles.

rationale: Moskva dead: 17 declared vs about 40.
resolution: The court declared dead only some of the missing; the higher figure is hearsay from a relative.

rationale: Different totals for Russian gains in 2025: 4,336 km² (DeepState) and 4,831 km² (CSIS) against about 4,700 km² (ISW).
resolution: Different mappers' methods and area accounting; all fall within about 10% of each other.

rationale: British intelligence's ~500,000 Russian killed (to Sep 2026) is hard to reconcile with CSIS's 275,000-325,000 killed (to Dec 2025) even allowing nine more months, though the casualty totals are consistent.
resolution: Different end dates and a different assumed killed-to-wounded ratio (about 1:3 vs 1:4).

rationale: Radio Svoboda gives 27 km² of Russian gains for July 2026, while the computed DeepStateMap value is 36 km².
resolution: Radio Svoboda's own calculation versus DeepState's published map for the same month; the gap reflects a different tracker, cutoff or netting method, not a change on the ground.

rationale: ISW data show 201 km² of Ukrainian gains in one week after the Starlink cutoff, while DeepState versions give only 48 km² of Ukrainian recapture for all of February 2026.
resolution: Different mappers; the week straddles late January and early February, the source has a date error, and DeepState publishes Ukrainian gains late.

rationale: Zelensky's 46,000 Ukrainian killed (February 2025) is far below CSIS's 100,000–140,000 killed to December 2025, a gap that ten months cannot plausibly explain.
resolution: Zelensky counts confirmed killed only, excluding missing; CSIS estimates likely dead including many of the missing. The periods also differ by ten months.

rationale: DeepState's 2025 peak of 450–550 km² a month is below Slivochny Kapriz's 550–600 km² a month for 2025.
resolution: Slivochny Kapriz credits any area where Russian troops were seen; DeepState counts confirmed control.

rationale: Size of the 155th Naval Infantry Brigade: about 5,000 vs about 2,000.
resolution: A Ukrainian claim that may count reinforcements over time vs Kyiv Post's full-strength estimate.

rationale: The January 2024 Avdiivka pipe is 1.3-1.4 m wide in Ukrainian reporting but 0.5 m in the Russian milblogger claim.
resolution: Russian channels may describe a different conduit or exaggerate the feat; Ukrainska Pravda's dimensions come from Ukrainian sources.

rationale: Moskva dead: 37 vs 1.
resolution: An unnamed Russian source vs the MoD's official figure, which likely understates by listing many as missing.

rationale: The DeepState-derived 134 km² and the UK MoD's 143 km² for Russian gains in March 2025 differ.
resolution: Different assessors with different mapping methods; the gap is small.

rationale: Monthly Russian gains in 2025 given as 450–550 km² (DeepState) vs 550–600 km² (Slivochny Kapriz).
resolution: Slivochny Kapriz credits any area where Russian troops were seen, inflating gains relative to DeepState's control-based mapping.

rationale: On 12 August 2024 ISW assessed about 800 km² of claimed Ukrainian advance in Kursk, while Syrskyi claimed about 1,000 km² held.
resolution: Syrskyi's is an official claim; ISW counts only advances it can corroborate and notes that not all claimed area is controlled.

rationale: DeepState reports 36 km² and Radio Svoboda 27 km² of Russian gains for July 2026.
resolution: Radio Svoboda's figure is not DeepState's own July report; the computed DeepState series also gives 36 km², so 27 is likely an error or a different source.

rationale: Military Chronicle claimed only one Tu-95MS lost at Olenya, while the "other sources" it relayed gave 8 Tu-95MS lost.
resolution: The one-loss figure is a minimising Russian milblogger line about Olenya; the eight comes from unnamed other sources and may cover all bases.

rationale: The DeepState-derived 134 km² and the UK MoD's 143 km² for Russian gains in March 2025 differ.
resolution: Different assessors with different mapping methods; the gap is small.

rationale: Analysts put Vivaldi gains at more than 200 and up to about 240 km², the 3rd Corps at 125 km².
resolution: The corps counts ground it confirms as cleared/liberated; mappers measure the wider area of changed control.

rationale: Length of the Kupiansk pipeline route: about 10 km vs 15 km.
resolution: Possibly different measures: the walk inside the pipe vs the full run from the Russian rear.

rationale: Ukrainian troops' 5:1 (8-9:1 at worst) shell ratio in early 2024 conflicts with officials' 1:10 for February 2024.
resolution: Frontline anecdotes from particular sectors vs an aggregate official figure; the worst-case local ratio is close to 1:10.

rationale: Dead in the 14 Jan 2024 A-50U: 11–12 vs about 15.
resolution: A Russian blogger vs an unnamed US officer; the crew size is uncertain.

rationale: The 3rd Corps claims 125 km² retaken in Vivaldi, outside mappers 200-240 km².
resolution: The corps counts ground it confirms as cleared/liberated; mappers measure the wider area of changed control.

rationale: Ukrainian troops' 5:1 (8-9:1 at worst) shell ratio in early 2024 conflicts with officials' 1:10 for February 2024.
resolution: Frontline anecdotes from particular sectors vs an aggregate official figure; the worst-case local ratio is close to 1:10.

rationale: Radio Svoboda's 27 km² and DeepState's 36 km² of Russian gains for July 2026 conflict.
resolution: Radio Svoboda's figure is likely an error or a different source; DeepState's own report and the computed series give 36 km².

rationale: Russians in Kupiansk in Dec 2025: about 500 with 100 trapped vs 300 falling to about 50.
resolution: Different units' estimates at different points in December.

rationale: DeepState's 36 km² and Radio Svoboda's 27 km² of Russian gains for July 2026 conflict.
resolution: Radio Svoboda's figure is likely an error or a different source; DeepState's own report and the computed series give 36 km².

rationale: The 3rd Corps reports 75 km² cleared and 10 km² liberated in Vivaldi phase 1, against OSINT estimates of more than 200 km².
resolution: The corps reports only ground it confirms as cleared/liberated; OSINT mappers measure the wider area of changed control.

rationale: The Atlantic Council's more than 200 km² retaken within five days of the Starlink cut conflicts with only 48 km² of Ukrainian recapture computed from DeepState for all of February 2026.
resolution: Different mappers; the counteroffensive began on 29 January, and DeepState publishes Ukrainian gains late.

rationale: For Avdiivka in February 2024, Ukrainian troops report a 5:1 Russian shell advantage while another report gives 1:10.
resolution: Different sources and days: 1:10 likely reflects the worst days or Foka's artillery-and-ammunition odds in the final weeks, versus a typical early-February rate.

rationale: A US estimate gives 13,000 Russian killed and wounded at Avdiivka in October–December 2023, while Shtupun implies about 20,000 on the Avdiivka axis in two months.
resolution: Ukrainian command claim versus a US intelligence estimate; slightly different periods.

rationale: Moskva dead: 1 vs 37.
resolution: The MoD's official figure lists many as missing; an unnamed Russian source gives the higher toll.

rationale: Ukrainian troops' 5:1 (8-9:1 at worst) shell ratio in early February 2024 conflicts with officials' 1:10 for February 2024.
resolution: Frontline anecdotes from particular sectors vs an aggregate official figure; the worst-case local ratio is close to 1:10.

rationale: 31 Dec 2024 Magura engagement: two Mi-8s downed vs one downed and one hit that reached its airfield.
resolution: HUR's later claim vs the initial reporting; the second helicopter's fate is uncertain.

rationale: CSIS puts Ukrainian dead at 100,000–140,000 to December 2025, far beyond Zelensky's 46,000 killed in February 2025, a gap that ten months cannot plausibly explain.
resolution: Zelensky counts confirmed killed only, excluding missing; CSIS estimates likely dead including many of the missing. The periods also differ by ten months.

rationale: US officials estimated up to about 20 aircraft hit in Spiderweb, while the SBU claimed 41 bombers hit.
resolution: US officials' estimate from imagery versus the SBU's own claim, which counts every aircraft it says it struck.

rationale: A-50 fleet and availability: 3 of 6 vs about 5 of 10.
resolution: Southern Command may count only modernised active airframes; TWZ estimates the whole fleet.

rationale: Ukrainian troops reported a 5:1 shell ratio at Avdiivka in early 2024, while Foka put artillery odds at 1:10 in the final weeks.
resolution: Anecdotal ratios from different units and weeks; 8–9:1 at worst approaches Foka's figure.

rationale: A's 70,000 UMPK kits ordered for 2025 (RUSI) conflicts with HUR's claim of more than 100,000 a year.
resolution: RUSI counts kits ordered; HUR cites planned production (120,000 for 2025).

rationale: BBC reports 117 drones launched in Spiderweb while Butusov says 116 became airborne.
resolution: Minor count difference; one drone may have failed to launch, or sources count differently.

rationale: Mediazona/BBC's estimate of 438,000-535,000 Russian dead conflicts with CSIS's 275,000-325,000 killed.
resolution: Different methods (Mediazona's inheritance-register extrapolation vs CSIS assessment) and probably different cut-off dates.

rationale: Zelensky's 55,000 Ukrainian killed by February 2026 is well below CSIS's 100,000-140,000 killed by December 2025.
resolution: Zelensky counts confirmed killed and lists the missing separately; CSIS estimates likely dead including many of the missing.

rationale: ISW's about 305 km² retaken by Ukraine at Kupiansk in late December 2025 conflicts with only 21 km² of Ukrainian recapture computed from DeepState for December 2025.
resolution: The computed series is dated by publication and DeepState withholds Ukrainian gains for OPSEC; ISW's assessment also differs in method.

rationale: Kirby's figure implies roughly 10,000 Wagner dead since December, against RUSI's 19,547 Wagner dead at Bakhmut.
resolution: RUSI counts the whole Bakhmut campaign from Wagner records; Kirby gave a US intelligence estimate for December-April only.

rationale: Size of Russia's A-50 fleet: 6 aircraft vs 10.
resolution: Southern Command may count only active modernised airframes; Militarnyi counts all airframes, including stored ones.

rationale: Moskva crew rescued: 58 vs 396.
resolution: Ukrainian NSDC vs Russian MoD claims; each side has motives.

rationale: Operational A-50s in Jan 2024: 8 vs about 5.
resolution: UKDI may count airworthy airframes, while TWZ counts those available at any one time.

rationale: Russia's claimed 6,000 km² of 2025 gains conflicts with trackers' 4,300-4,800 km².
resolution: Russian official claims include territory not confirmed by independent mappers.

rationale: Dead in the 14 Jan 2024 A-50U: 11 vs about 15.
resolution: ASN record vs an unnamed US officer; the crew size is uncertain.

rationale: RUSI's 70,000 UMPK kits for 2025 conflicts with HUR's claim of more than 100,000 a year.
resolution: RUSI counts kits ordered; HUR cites planned production (120,000 for 2025).

rationale: Butusov says 116 drones became airborne while the SBU says 117 were launched.
resolution: Minor count difference; the official 117 may include a drone that did not take off.

rationale: ISW's net Russian change for March-September 2026 (-195 or +361 km²) is hard to reconcile with DeepState-derived +620 km² for February-September 2026.
resolution: Different mappers and methods (ISW advanced/infiltration categories vs DeepState line), and the DeepState window includes February.

rationale: The same brigade gives Russian odds at Avdiivka of 1:12 and 7:1 for the same final weeks.
resolution: Foka's 1:12 refers to infantry in the final weeks; the 7:1 may be an overall or earlier force ratio.

rationale: Rival accounts of the Act 1 charge: 21 t TNT-equivalent RDX vs about 10 t of rocket fuel.
resolution: SBU account vs Russian case file.

rationale: The same Avdiivka pipe is described as an empty 1.3–1.4 m service-water main versus a flooded 0.5 m drainage pipe.
resolution: The Russian accounts are unverified and may dramatise the infiltration or describe a different conduit; the Ukrainian-side technical description is better sourced.

rationale: HUR puts North Korean casualties at more than 7,000 in June 2026, while the NIS and UK put them at about 6,000 over the same period.
resolution: Different intelligence services with different methods; HUR's figure is the higher and less conservative one.

rationale: The historical floor of about 10 heavy bombers destroyed conflicts with Military Chronicle's claim that only one Tu-95MS was lost.
resolution: A pro-Russian blog minimising losses, against imagery-based counts by several analysts.

rationale: Length of the Kupiansk pipeline route: about 10 km vs 15 km.
resolution: Possibly different measures: the walk inside the pipe vs the full run from the Russian rear.

rationale: One Oryx report as of 9 June 2023 logs 3 Leopard 2A6 lost near Mala Tokmachka, another logs 2 Leopards lost.
resolution: Oryx's list was updated during 9 June; the two reports likely use different snapshots.

rationale: The DeepState-derived +134 km² and ISW's about 203 km² for Russian gains in March 2025 conflict.
resolution: Different mappers and methods; ISW's assessed advances are usually larger than DeepState's.

rationale: 200-201 km² of Ukrainian gains in the first week after the Starlink cutoff conflicts with only 48 km² of Ukrainian recapture computed from DeepState for all of February 2026.
resolution: Different mappers; the week straddles late January and early February, and DeepState publishes Ukrainian gains late.

rationale: HUR claims over 7,000 North Korean casualties, while the NIS and UK put them at about 6,000 in February–June 2026.
resolution: Different intelligence services with different methods; HUR's figure is the higher one.

rationale: The corps claims 75 km² cleared plus 10 km² liberated in Vivaldi phase 1, while OSINT estimates exceed 200 km².
resolution: The corps counts only formally cleared or liberated ground; outside OSINT mappers count all area where Russian control ended, including grey zone.

rationale: NIS/UK put North Korean casualties at about 6,000 while HUR put them above 7,000 in the same months.
resolution: Different agencies' estimates; HUR's June 2026 figure may be a later or broader count than the NIS/UK one.

rationale: Ukrainian dead in the May 2022 Zmiinyi assault: about 10 vs more than 50.
resolution: Ukrainian reporting vs a Russian MoD claim that is likely inflated.

rationale: For Avdiivka in February 2024, Foka gives 1:10 odds in artillery and ammunition while Ukrainian troops report a 5:1 shell advantage.
resolution: Foka describes the final weeks before withdrawal; the 5:1 figure is from early February, and different units and sources report.

rationale: The SBU claims 41 aircraft hit, while US officials estimated up to about 20 hit.
resolution: The SBU counts every aircraft it says it struck; US officials' estimate is independent and more conservative.

rationale: The SBU claims 41 aircraft hit while BBC Verify counted 12 damaged or destroyed.
resolution: The SBU counts every aircraft it says it hit, including light damage; BBC counts only damage visible in satellite imagery.

rationale: RUSI gives 19,547 Wagner dead at Bakhmut for December 2022-May 2023, while Kirby put all Russian dead since December at about 20,000, nearly half of them Wagner (about 10,000).
resolution: RUSI's figure likely covers the whole Bakhmut battle from mid-2022 and draws on Wagner's own records; Kirby's US estimate covers only December-April.

rationale: The 3rd Corps claims 125 km² in Vivaldi, while outside mappers put the gains at over 200 and up to about 240 km².
resolution: The corps counts ground it confirms as cleared/liberated; mappers measure the wider area of changed control.

rationale: Zelensky's 55,000 Ukrainian killed by February 2026 is well below CSIS's 100,000-140,000 killed by December 2025.
resolution: Zelensky counts confirmed killed and lists the missing separately; CSIS estimates likely dead including many of the missing.

rationale: SBU says 117 drones were used in Spiderweb while Butusov says 116 were launched.
resolution: Minor count difference; one drone may have been used but not launched, or sources count differently.

rationale: DeepState's 4,336 km² for 2025 conflicts with Slivochny Kapriz's 550-600 km² a month (about 6,600-7,200 km² a year).
resolution: Slivochny Kapriz credits any area where Russian troops were seen, including infiltration; DeepState marks control.

rationale: Same Sudzha-pipe force size, about 100 vs over 600.
resolution: Ukrainian reporting vs Gerasimov's claim; the Russian figure is likely inflated for propaganda.

rationale: Two readings of the same January 2025 Syrskyi briefing differ: the Guardian has 15,000 wounded or missing in addition to 7,000 killed, the other has 15,000 casualties in total.
resolution: Two outlets read one briefing differently; the total is either 15,000 or about 22,000.

rationale: Butusov says 116 drones were launched in Spiderweb while the SBU's official figure is 117.
resolution: Minor count difference; the official 117 may include a drone that did not take off.
